cards.note: The plugin never used repository-plugins.repositories: it is already an npm-shaped bundle installed through the single official profile path (`dsh plugin --profile h1m add`, verified exit 0).
Host-plane package with no client half, so no legacy dshClient/dsh.plugin.json manifest exists to rename.
No Web Client bundle or client entry; the client-modules scan contract never reaches this package.
The only consumed service (`llm`) is declared in `inject`; no ctx.get/property access for an undeclared service remains, so alpha.2 strict injection is satisfied (cold boot exit 0).
No optional host service is probed; the single dependency is hard and profile-guaranteed, so no weak ctx.get fallback is warranted.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state from event fields.
No self-rendering client half and no ctx.sessions usage; nothing to aggregate in a Node half.
No task/run output tailing; the removed tasks.peek was never used.
No httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone identifiers anywhere in the tree; the plugin owns no web route or job listener.
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image output or persisted image metadata in this plugin.
read_image is neither registered, wrapped, parsed nor snapshot-tested here.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor or attachment cache to migrate.

Host-plane apiProxy consumer migrated to the domain service behind the deleted facade: `inject: ["llm"]` + `ctx.llm.listProviders()`. Verified against dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2: migrated bundle boots exit 0, while both the baseline `apiProxy` and the memo's `remote` injection fail closed with `pending (waiting for service: ...)` + `dsh: 1 entry did not activate`.
Target is alpha.2 (A2-01 restored ignorable) and the plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents.
No host-source patch and no import from internal session-view paths.
The plugin does not read profile files or wrap a launcher; verification used the runtime DSH_HOME, the target profile and the official launcher.
The plugin only writes its own stderr diagnostics; it is not a headless wrapper or a stdout/stderr parser.
No PTC/Code Mode presentation, PTC preset, dispatch waterfall or related type usage.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch policy plugin; the bundle patch inserts one plugin row and nothing else.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route, browser page or /api surface; the channel auth gate does not touch this plugin.
Not a model-provider plugin and ships no settings page, so the optional login-configuration capability is not adopted.
Ships no localization resources and carries no custom i18n patch.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface.
Informational host-side privacy behavior of the official DeepSeek adapter; the plugin only reads provider facts and needs no code change. Deployment maintainers own the privacy decision.
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workaround exists to delete.
session-log-deepseek incremental upload is a deployment choice; this bundle does not enable or configure it.
No browser half, so no boot-manifest entry or token/auth URL acceptance surface exists for this plugin.
Does not register structured-question answerers and does not consume userQuestions.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions and no agent-presets roots to switch to probing.
No import from @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/message; first-token/TPS detection is absent.
This bundle patch only inserts its own row; it does not restate or reuse the dsh-base telemetry/package-inventory composition rows.
Does not depend on or import @earendil-works/pi-ai; no second-instance risk.
Host-only package: no @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime dependency, import or dsh.client.inject entry.
No Web Client half; the host-plane bundle row name already equals the package.json name, so the id==package-name rule is satisfied.
No session timeline or user-message content reads; the SessionBinding window is not needed.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall, shortcuts, selection).
Does not render MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlocks from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives.
No client ctx.connection.api usage and no history/transcript reads.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors are constructed, and the subagent/descriptor event is not consumed.
No ctx.workspaces navigation, startSession, pickDirectory or directory-listing calls.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable marker has no producer here.
Host plane only: no ctx.remote unary calls and no RemoteResult/RemoteError handling.

Dependency graph migrated for the cohort: the dead @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency was removed and peers re-floored (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` ^4.0.1, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` ^0.1.2-alpha.2). Install verified in an isolated profile with the single package manager (pnpm) the official path uses; this package intentionally ships no lockfile.
No startup wrapper or CI matrix in this repository, so no Node 24.0-24.11.1 workaround exists to remove.
Does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate PluginInventorySnapshot.
No client Remote; ctx.remote.$host.home/isLoopback is not read.

Does not compose its own profile or mount dsh-tool-todo/dsh-tool-subagent/dsh-agent/dsh-terminal-bash individually; it is a leaf bundle inserted into a dsh-base profile that already mounts session-projection.
No ctx.settings register/update/get usage and no settings namespace declaration.
